result.answer:
Based on the Office of Kaiju Affairs' claims fee rules, here's the answer:

**You will still need to pay the ¥12,000 assessment fee for this second claim.**

**The rule** (Claims FAQ, "Fee waivers" section):
> "Claimants with two or more **approved** claims from separate incidents within any rolling 12-month period are exempt from the ¥12,000 assessment fee. The waiver is applied automatically at lodgement; no separate application is required."
— *Claims FAQ, https://office-of-kaiju-affairs.vercel.app/claims/faq/*

**Why it doesn't apply yet:** The waiver is evaluated *at lodgement*, based on how many claims you already have **approved**. Right now you have only **one** approved claim (the March incident) — your upcoming claim for the incident three weeks ago hasn't been assessed or approved yet, so it doesn't count toward the "two or more approved" threshold at the moment you file it. Since you only meet the "1 approved claim" mark, not "two or more," the automatic waiver doesn't trigger for this filing.

**Practical takeaway:** Pay the ¥12,000 fee when you lodge this second claim. If it's approved, you'll then have two approved claims from separate incidents within the rolling 12-month window — meaning if a *third* incident occurs within that same 12-month period, the assessment fee for that future claim would be automatically waived.

One additional note from the fee schedule (*/claims/fees/*): regardless of the repeat-claimant waiver, "the assessment fee is refunded in full where the final award exceeds ¥1,000,000" — so if your damage award for this claim is large enough, you could get the fee back that way even though the repeat-claimant waiver itself doesn't apply this time.
